title: Determinant-line isomorphism for an exact sequence of finite projective modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{p}W\to0$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules, meaning that $i$ is injective, $p$ is surjective and $\operatorname{im}(i)=\ker(p)$. Assume $U,V,W$ are direct summands of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For any such module $E$, its determinant module $\det_R(E)$ is obtained on finite free localizations [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] by taking the top exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and identifying these rank-one modules on overlaps using the top exterior powers of change-of-basis maps; the determinant of the zero module is $R$. These local modules define an invertible $R$-module (a finite projective module locally free of rank one). There is a canonical isomorphism $\gamma_{i,p}:\det_R(U)\otimes_R\det_R(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_R(V)$. On a localization where $U,W$ have bases $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_s$, its formula is
$$\gamma_{i,p}((u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_r)\otimes(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_s))=i(u_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge i(u_r)\wedge\widetilde w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widetilde w_s,$$
where $p(\widetilde w_j)=w_j$. This formula is independent of the lifts and bases and commutes with further localization; it includes $r=0$ and $s=0$.
